title: Bidirectional enrichment bridge: canonicalize legacy chat completion I/O
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: A set of legacy clients rely on the OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response shapes and streaming semantics. When routed through Redwood's runtime we must preserve functional equivalence for tool/function calls, streaming envelope boundaries, structured JSON outputs, and idempotency semantics while also exposing Redwood-native telemetry and cost signals.

Goal: Implement a bidirectional enrichment bridge that canonicalizes incoming legacy chat-completion requests into Redwood's internal canonical conversation format, enriches/annotates streams with provenance and span IDs, and translates outgoing responses (including function_call events and structured outputs) back into the legacy API shape. The bridge should be feature-flagged with a transparent pass-through fallback and support a staged canary rollout.

Technical approach:
- Inbound: normalize message arrays, detect and lift legacy function_call hints in messages into a canonical tool-invocation intent. Attach idempotency_token and request provenance (region, model_variant) to metadata.
- Streaming: implement a lightweight re-framer that converts Redwood stream frames into OpenAI-compatible delta chunks while preserving atomic tool-call frames. Handle partial JSON fragments for structured outputs via a buffer window with bounded memory.
- Outbound function/tool calling: map Redwood tool invocation results back to the legacy function_call response shape, including argument serialization, tool provenance, and an explicit "invocation_id" that maps to Redwood span IDs. Support both synchronous and async tool responses via intermediate 102-like progress frames (emulated in the legacy chunk stream).
- Structured outputs: validate and coerce Redwood structured-output objects to legacy top-level content fields where required; emit a best-effort schema-conversion warning in the response metadata if coercion was lossy.
- Telemetry: emit traceable span IDs in both directions; expose a lightweight token-level cost estimate header for downstream billing/console.
- Safety/perf: provide adaptive path that skips deep schema validation under heavy load (configurable threshold) to maintain latency SLOs.

Tradeoffs and constraints:
- Fidelity vs latency: full canonicalization and schema validation increases p95 latency; we mitigate via a configurable fast-path for latency-critical routes.
- CPU overhead: enrichment and JSON reassembly add CPU and memory; we will measure and gate via canary.
- Semantic edge-cases: some legacy clients assume specific ordering of delta chunks; we must preserve ordering but cannot replicate all buggy client behavior. Document known mismatches in rollout notes.
acceptance_criteria: Inbound legacy request shapes are deterministically mapped to Redwood canonical conversation objects in >99.9% of synthetic test cases
Streaming re-framer produces OpenAI-compatible chunk sequence with no dropped tool-call frames under normal load
Tool/function-call round trip preserves arguments and returns an invocation_id that maps to Redwood trace IDs
Canary rollout support: feature flag toggles behavior per-customer and per-route
Automated regression suite (unit + integration) covering JSON fragment reassembly, idempotency tokens, and overflow cases
Performance: additional p95 latency introduced by the bridge is <= 40ms on our internal baseline for typical requests (unless fast-path enabled)
Telemetry: every bridged request emits span_id and provenance headers consumed by Console traces
comments: 2025-02-25 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after spike; initial requirements captured from support tickets where customers reported broken tool-calls when switching to Redwood runtime.

2025-02-27 - Liam Chen: Spike done. Prototype re-framer works but fails on interleaved partial JSON from some legacy clients. We will buffer up to 8KB and attempt incremental parse; fallback to pass-through if buffer boundary exceeded.

2025-03-01 - Design review: PM (Sofia Martinez) requested explicit migration notes and an opt-out header for customers who prefer raw pass-through. Also asked for an opt-in telemetry header to avoid PII leakage.

2025-03-02 - Security review kickoff: Security team requested threat model doc and ensured function_call arguments are not accidentally logged. Added requirement to scrub sensitive keys from arguments before sending to Console by default.

2025-03-04 - PR feedback: Code reviewer (Ravi Shah) suggested moving schema coercion logic into a pluggable module and adding a metrics counter for lossy-coercions. Also asked for clearer unit tests for streaming chunk reassembly edge cases.

2025-03-05 - Performance test run: Canary worker with 10k qps synthetic test shows CPU increase ~12% and p95 latency +28ms on medium payloads with validation on. Fast-path toggle reduces p95 delta to +6ms. Proceeding with staged canary.
Next steps: finish PR addressing review comments, add threat-model doc link, create migration playbook for Customer Success, schedule canary for subset of Fortune 50 customers next week.
